One map, one color scale, and the entire political history of the last 250 years: which countries are democracies in 2025 — and why the pattern looks the way it does.

a thread 🧵🗺️

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)

1/ V-Dem's classification splits the world into four bands: liberal democracy, electoral democracy, electoral autocracy, and closed autocracy. Most of the map isn't fully democratic OR fully closed — it's the murky 'electoral autocracy' middle, orange on the map.
2/ Western Europe, North America, Australia and Japan form a near-solid democratic bloc — but this is historically very recent. As late as 1900, not one country on Earth had full adult suffrage.

3/ The deep red band — closed autocracy — runs through North Africa, the Gulf, and parts of Central Asia and East Asia. Many of these states still hold elections; per Our World in Data, the modern norm is autocracies that fake democratic form without its substance.

4/ Democracy has come in waves, not a straight line: an early wave after WWI, a bigger one after WWII decolonization, and a huge 'third wave' after 1989 when the USSR collapsed and Eastern Europe flipped almost overnight.

5/ But waves also recede. Political scientists have tracked global democratic backsliding since roughly the mid-2010s — more countries moving from electoral democracy toward electoral autocracy than the reverse.

6/ The real lesson: 'democracy' and 'autocracy' aren't a light switch, they're a dimmer — most governments sit in the dim middle, not at either end.

What surprised you about your region's shade? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
